walkthroughs.body_html: Cosmic rays are about 90% protons, 9% helium nuclei and 1% electrons. The highest-energy ones exceed 10^20 eV — far beyond any human accelerator. Sources are still debated.
A primary cosmic ray collides with an air molecule and triggers an air shower of secondary particles. The Pierre Auger Observatory samples these showers over 3000 km^2 in Argentina.

Only the optical and radio bands pass through the full atmosphere; infrared has partial windows; X-rays and gamma rays need to be observed from space. This shapes where each kind of telescope is placed.
